question: Asked whether San Diego or San Antonio had more people, why did German students beat American ones?
answer: Because most had heard only of San Diego, and picked it. Goldstein and Gigerenzer found every German student right, against about 62% of Americans, who knew both names and had to reason. Recognition worked because bigger cities are talked about more. A gut shortcut is good exactly where what comes to mind tracks the answer.
move: Trust a shortcut only where what you notice is linked to what is true.
ask: Where do I lean on what I have heard of, and does fame there really track quality?
reference: Goldstein & Gigerenzer, Models of ecological rationality: the recognition heuristic, Psychological Review, 2002
